gallery.title: Sunburst & Radial Dendrogram
gallery.description: Two views of the same 55-node organization share one polar plane: a Radial Dendrogram above and a weighted Sunburst below, each spanning 180°.

file.name: tree.csv
file.description: One row per organization node. node_id identifies the node, parent_id identifies its parent (empty for the root), and weight determines Sunburst sector size. The 55 nodes span six levels below the root; label and metric_1–metric_5 remain available but are not bound.

bindings.role: Sunburst node ID · Radial Dendrogram node ID
Parent ID in both hierarchy blocks

gallery.composition: Start with the two independently bound blocks. Apply angular Concat with shared Radius (R): both views use one center and the same hierarchy-depth scale, with the Radial Dendrogram on the upper 180° and the Sunburst on the lower 180°. Labels are hidden to keep the structure readable; node details remain in tooltips.

editorHelp.introduction: The Sunburst and Radial Dendrogram are already bound to the same hierarchy. Join them at an angular edge to make two halves of one circle.

steps.title: Drag the hierarchy to the angular edge
steps.target: Sunburst’s outer angular Concat sector just below the right-hand seam
steps.action: Hold the Radial Dendrogram and move the pointer to the small sector outside the Sunburst, just below the right-hand seam where its full-circle sweep ends. This sector sits beyond the ring-shaped drop zone. Release only when the highlighted sector reads Concat · share RADIUS.
steps.result: Angular Concat shares hierarchy depth: the Sunburst occupies the lower half and the Radial Dendrogram the upper half.

steps.title: Check the shared circle
steps.target: One center, with a 180° half for each view
steps.action: Check that the trees meet at one center. If you made concentric rings, use Undo and repeat the drag onto the angular sector labeled Concat · share RADIUS; the ring-shaped zone shares ANGLE instead.
steps.result: The finished layout has branches above and colored Sunburst arcs below.
